newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices recover from lows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices recover from lows.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices bounced off the week's lows Wednesday, as colder weather moved into the Midwest and the futures market edged higher, sources said.
Prices on the Gulf Coast pipes regained about six cents to the low-$3 per mmBtu area, still almost a $1 under January indices.
Similarly in south Texas, prices rose by about five cents to the $2.89-2.94 range, as normal to slightly below-normal temperatures blanketed the region.
As of 1440 EST, February was 2.4 cents higher at $2.94.
"It's still winter. Once prices (at Henry Hub) got below $3, people got a little nervous," one trader said.
The strength in the Gulf boosted Midcontinent prices by about one to two cents to the $2.85-2.90 range.
Despite cooler temperatures in the Midcontinent, forecasters are calling for a return of above-normal temperatures by early next week.
Chicago city-gate values were talked a few cents higher in the $3.20s.
In west Texas, Permian prices edged about five cents higher to the mid-$2.80s.

Adding support to the market was news that Southern California Edison's 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit may not restart as scheduled on February 8. The restart from a maintenance outage may be delayed by 10-15 days.
This news also put some upward pressure on California border prices, as traders reported closing deals at Topock in the $2.80-2.95 range.
In the East, where stocks are well above year-ago levels, prices eased into the $3.20-3.50 range, down about 15-20 cents from Tuesday.
Withdrawal estimates for tonight's American Gas Association storage report ranged anywhere from 150 to 225 bcf, with the bulk of the expectations in the 190-200 range.
